text:
lina: Acme Health reporting a spike of 429s from their dedicated pool right after their plan bump went live ~03:12 UTC. Customer says it started immediately after billing confirmed the new tier.

sara: Thanks Lina. Any error payloads or sample request ids?

lina: Pasting one 429 we saw from their app: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","tenant":"acme-health","rate_key":"tenant:acme-health:dedicated","quota_window":"1h","allowed":1200,"used":1201}`

lina: They also sent a curl repro: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-...' \ 
  -d '{"model":"mix-small","input":"summarize...","tenant_id":"acme-health"}'
```

nate: @lina can you confirm which dedicated pool they are on? quietpool-3 or reserved-42?

lina: quietpool-3. I've captured request ids: `r-2026-03-17-0012` and `r-2026-03-17-0019`.

autoscale-bot: [autoscale] quietpool-3 scaled from 8->12 GPUs at 03:10:45 UTC, warmup ramp policy in effect (+20s per GPU).

nate: Hmm, autoscale happened *before* the billing plan change completed? Could be a warmup window mismatch causing pacing to apply.

sara: Customer says they were allowed higher throughput in old plan already; plan bump should increase per-tenant rate units. Maybe the quota migration applied with the wrong denom (minutes vs hours) -> effective limit lower than expected.

ryan: I'm seeing the tenant's quota record in the quota-store: `tenant:acme-health -> units: 7200, denom: HOUR` (should be units: 7200, denom: MINUTE) — looks like denom was set to HOUR during the plan migration job.

nate: That would make a 7200/HOUR -> 2/min, huge drop vs intended 7200/MIN. That explains immediate 429s.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rollback flag set for migration-job v2026.03.17-quota-migrate by ryan at 03:28 UTC.

lina: Repro steps I used to confirm: 1) hit their tenant with a steady 30 req/s for 5m, 2) observe token counters and 429s in response, 3) check quota-store snapshot. Logs attached above.

nate: Two failure modes stacked: denom misconfig + autoscale warmup/pacing windows. Even after increasing pool size, the tenant hit the artificially low hourly denom and got penalized.

sara: Agreed. Immediate remediation: ryan temporarily bumped the tenant override to units: 432000/ MINUTE (equiv to previous intended capacity) — that stopped 429s at 03:40 UTC. Customer reports normal behavior again. :thumbsup:

ryan: Follow-up tasks I'm creating: 1) add assert in plan-migration job to validate denom field (MINUTE vs HOUR) 2) add preflight comparison between old plan-derived limits and new values 3) add a migration dry-run flag in production pipeline.

nate: Also let's consider changing warmup pacing to be less aggressive on quietpools when per-tenant quotas are being updated, or block quota flips during a scale-up window.

lina: Customer notified and thanked us; they've asked for postmortem and timeline.

sara: I'll draft a short incident timeline and include the repro steps + fix. Assigning follow-ups to @ryan and @nate.

ryan: Will open PRs for the migration fix and an integration test that compares post-migrate effective rate vs expected rates.

nate: One more item — add a temporary metric alert for large denom changes (HOUR <-> MINUTE) on migration pipeline so we catch these config flips early.

lina: Closing the support escalation ticket after publishing the customer note. Leaving thread open for follow-up PR links.

ops-bot: [note] customer-acme-health case #25342 marked RESOLVED at 03:55 UTC.
